units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Tens and ones, adding and subtracting
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Mathematics: Numbers, Operations and Relationships (place value of 2-digit numbers; add and subtract to 99; word problems)
units.intention: Today I am using tens and ones to add and subtract bigger numbers.
units.prompt: Did you work with the tens first or the ones first?

lesson.say: The number 47 has 4 tens and 7 ones. Four tens is forty, and seven ones is seven.
lesson.html:
🔟 🔟 🔟 🔟 🔹 🔹 🔹 🔹 🔹 🔹 🔹

47 = 40 + 7. The 4 is worth 40.

lesson.say: To add 32 and 25, add the tens: 30 and 20 make 50. Add the ones: 2 and 5 make 7. Together that is 57.
lesson.html:
30 + 20 = 50→2 + 5 = 7→50 + 7 = 57

Break the numbers into tens and ones, then put them back together.

lesson.say: To work out 68 take away 23, take away the tens: 60 take away 20 is 40. Take away the ones: 8 take away 3 is 5. The answer is 45.
lesson.html:
60 − 20 = 40→8 − 3 = 5→40 + 5 = 45

Subtract the tens, then the ones.

example.q: There are 14 children on one bus and 23 children on another bus. How many children altogether?

questions.q: How many tens are in 63?
hints: The first digit shows the tens.
questions.explain: 63 has 6 tens and 3 ones.

questions.q: What is 41 plus 26?
What is 79 take away 35?
A farmer has 58 sheep. He sells 20. How many are left?
Which number has 8 tens and 2 ones?
questions.explain: 8 tens and 2 ones is 82.

questions.q: Put the numbers in order, smallest first.

units.parent: Your child used tens and ones to add and subtract numbers up to 99.
units.teacher: Shows place value of 2-digit numbers and addition and subtraction to 99 by breaking down numbers.
units.done: Split numbers into tens and ones to add and subtract.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Equal groups and times
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Mathematics: Numbers, Operations and Relationships (repeated addition leading to multiplication; skip counting in 2s, 5s and 10s; grouping and sharing)
units.intention: Today I am learning that times means equal groups.
units.prompt: How did counting in groups help you?

lesson.say: Three plates with four cupcakes on each. That is three groups of four, which is twelve.
lesson.html:
🧁🧁🧁🧁   🧁🧁🧁🧁   🧁🧁🧁🧁

3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

lesson.say: Three groups of four can be written as three times four. Three times four equals twelve.
lesson.html:
4 + 4 + 4→=→3 × 4→=→12

The × sign means groups of.

lesson.say: Counting in twos, fives and tens helps us find answers fast. Five times two is ten. Five times five is twenty-five.
lesson.html:
2→4→6→8→10
5→10→15→20→25

Skip count to multiply.

example.q: A spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 2 spiders have?

questions.q: How many socks are in 4 pairs? A pair is 2.
questions.html: 🧦🧦 🧦🧦 🧦🧦 🧦🧦
questions.explain: 4 × 2 = 8 socks.

questions.q: What is 5 times 3?
Which is the same as 10 plus 10 plus 10?
Each hand has 5 fingers. How many fingers on 6 hands?
questions.explain: 6 × 5 = 30 fingers.

questions.q: Share 20 sweets equally into groups of 5. How many groups?
questions.explain: 20 shared into groups of 5 makes 4 groups.

units.parent: Your child learned that multiplying means equal groups and practised counting in 2s, 5s and 10s.
units.teacher: Shows repeated addition as multiplication, skip counting in 2s, 5s and 10s, and grouping.
units.done: Times means equal groups. Skip counting helps you multiply.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Halves, quarters and thirds
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Mathematics: Numbers, Operations and Relationships (fractions: halves, quarters, thirds and fifths; sharing leading to fractions)
units.intention: Today I am learning to share a whole into equal parts.
units.prompt: How did you check the parts were equal?

lesson.say: When we cut something into two equal parts, each part is one half.
lesson.html: 2 equal parts. Each part is one half.

lesson.say: When we cut something into four equal parts, each part is one quarter.
lesson.html: 4 equal parts. Each part is one quarter.

lesson.say: When we cut something into three equal parts, each part is one third. The parts must be equal.
lesson.html: 3 equal parts. Each part is one third.

example.q: Mum cuts a pizza into 4 equal slices. You eat 1 slice. What fraction did you eat?

questions.q: What fraction is shaded?
questions.html: <svg width="100%" style="max-width:300px" viewBox="0 0 300 44" role="img" aria-label="1 out of 2 equal parts shaded"><rect x="1" y="2" width="148" height="40" rx="4" fill="var(--shape-a)" stroke="var(--ink)" stroke-opacity="0.5"/><rect x="151" y="2" width="148" height="40" rx="4" fill="var(--surface)" stroke="var(--ink)" stroke-opacity="0.5"/></svg>
questions.explain: 1 of 2 equal parts is one half.

questions.q: What fraction is shaded?
questions.html: <svg width="100%" style="max-width:300px" viewBox="0 0 300 44" role="img" aria-label="1 out of 3 equal parts shaded"><rect x="1" y="2" width="98" height="40" rx="4" fill="var(--shape-a)" stroke="var(--ink)" stroke-opacity="0.5"/><rect x="101" y="2" width="98" height="40" rx="4" fill="var(--surface)" stroke="var(--ink)" stroke-opacity="0.5"/><rect x="201" y="2" width="98" height="40" rx="4" fill="var(--surface)" stroke="var(--ink)" stroke-opacity="0.5"/></svg>
questions.explain: 1 of 3 equal parts is one third.

questions.q: Half of 10 sweets is how many?
questions.explain: Half of 10 is 5.

questions.q: Which is bigger, one half or one quarter of the same cake?
hints: A half is 1 of 2 bigger pieces.
questions.explain: One half is bigger than one quarter.

questions.q: A quarter of 8 apples is how many?
questions.explain: A quarter of 8 is 2.

units.parent: Your child learned halves, quarters and thirds, and found half and a quarter of a group.
units.teacher: Shows recognition of unit fractions as equal parts of a whole and of a group.
units.done: Fractions are equal parts of a whole.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Telling the time
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Mathematics: Measurement (read 12-hour time in hours and half hours on analogue clocks; calendars and lengths of time)
units.intention: Today I am learning to read o'clock and half past on a clock.
units.prompt: How did the hands help you tell the time?

lesson.say: A clock has a short hand and a long hand. The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
lesson.html: The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.

lesson.say: When the long hand points to 12, it is o'clock. This clock shows three o'clock.
lesson.html: Long hand on 12 means o'clock. This is 3 o'clock.

lesson.say: When the long hand points to 6, it is half past. The short hand is halfway between two numbers. This clock shows half past four.
lesson.html: Long hand on 6 means half past. This is half past 4.

example.q: School starts at 8 o'clock. Where does the long hand point?
steps: O'clock means the long hand is on 12.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?

questions.q: What time does this clock show?

questions.explain: It is half past 2.

questions.q: How many minutes are in one hour?
hints: The long hand goes all the way round.
questions.explain: There are 60 minutes in one hour.

questions.q: It is 1 o'clock. What time will it be in one hour?
hints: The short hand moves to the next number.
questions.explain: One hour after 1 o'clock is 2 o'clock.

questions.q: Put the day in order.
hints: What happens first in the morning?
questions.explain: Wake up, school, then supper.

reflect.q: What helped you read the clock?
options: Looking at the long hand first

units.parent: Your child learned to read o'clock and half past on a clock. Ask them to read your kitchen clock.
units.teacher: Shows reading analogue time to the hour and half hour and simple elapsed time.
units.done: Long hand on 12 is o'clock. Long hand on 6 is half past.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Two letters, one sound
units.topic: Vowel digraphs ee, oo, ai, oa
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 English Home Language: Phonics (vowel digraphs such as ee, oo, ai, oa, ea; consonant digraphs sh, ch, th, wh)
units.intention: Today I am reading words where two letters make one sound.

lesson.say: Sometimes two letters make one sound. E and e together say ee, like in tree and see.
lesson.html:
tr-ee→s-ee→f-ee-t

🌳 👀 🦶

ee says one long sound.

lesson.say: O and o say oo, like in moon. A and i say ai, like in rain.
lesson.html:
m-oo-n→sp-oo-n
r-ai-n→s-ai-l

🌙 🥄 🌧️ ⛵

lesson.say: O and a say oa, like in boat. S and h say sh, like in ship.
lesson.html:
b-oa-t→g-oa-t
sh-i-p→f-i-sh

🚤 🐐 🚢 🐟

example.q: Read the word: s, oa, p. What is it?
steps: oa says the long o sound.

questions.q: Which word has the ee sound?
questions.explain: Bee has the ee sound.

questions.q: Which word has the oo sound like moon?
questions.explain: Spoon has the oo sound.

questions.q: Which letters make the sound in rain?
questions.explain: Rain has the ai sound.

questions.q: Which word starts with sh?
questions.explain: Shoe starts with sh.

questions.q: Sort by sound.
questions.explain: Green and sheep have ee. Coat and road have oa.

reflect.q: What helped you read the words?

units.parent: Your child read words where two letters make one sound, such as ee, oo, ai, oa and sh.
units.teacher: Shows decoding of vowel digraphs ee, oo, ai, oa and the consonant digraph sh.
units.done: Sometimes two letters work together to make one sound.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Question marks and exclamation marks
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 English Home Language: Language Structure and Use (full stop, question mark, exclamation mark, comma in a list)
units.intention: Today I am choosing the right mark to end a sentence.
units.prompt: How did you know which mark to use?

lesson.say: A telling sentence gives information. It ends with a full stop. The dog is brown.
lesson.html:
The dog is brown.

A telling sentence ends with a full stop.

lesson.say: An asking sentence asks a question. It ends with a question mark. Where is my bag?
lesson.html:
Where is my bag?

Asking words: who, what, where, when, why, how. Use a question mark.

lesson.say: When we feel something strongly, we use an exclamation mark. Watch out! What a big fish!
lesson.html:
Watch out!

What a big fish!

An exclamation mark shows surprise, excitement or danger.

example.q: Which mark ends this sentence? What is your name

questions.q: Which mark ends this sentence? How old are you
hints: Questions end with a question mark.
questions.explain: How old are you? It is a question.

questions.q: Which mark ends this sentence? I have a red bike
hints: Telling sentences end with a full stop.
questions.explain: I have a red bike. It is a telling sentence.

questions.q: Which mark ends this sentence? Help, the house is on fire
questions.explain: Help, the house is on fire! It shows danger.

questions.q: Where do the commas go? I like apples pears and grapes.
hints: Commas separate things in a list.
The list is apples, pears and grapes.
questions.explain: I like apples, pears and grapes.

questions.q: Sort the sentences.
hints: Can and where are asking words.
questions.explain: Can you swim? Where do you live? The sky is blue. We eat at six.

units.parent: Your child chose between full stops, question marks and exclamation marks, and used commas in a list.
units.teacher: Shows use of end punctuation by sentence type and commas in a list.
units.done: Telling sentences end with a full stop, questions with a question mark.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Yesterday, today and tomorrow
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 English Home Language: Language Structure and Use (present, past and future tense)
units.intention: Today I am learning how verbs change for yesterday, today and tomorrow.
units.prompt: Which words told you when it happened?

lesson.say: Things happening now are in the present tense. Today I play.
lesson.html:
Today→I play

Present tense: it is happening now.

lesson.say: Things that already happened are in the past tense. We often add e d. Yesterday I played.
lesson.html:
Yesterday→I played

Past tense: it already happened. Many verbs add -ed.

lesson.say: Things that will happen are in the future tense. We use will. Tomorrow I will play.
lesson.html:
Tomorrow→I will play

Future tense: it will happen.

example.q: Change to the past: Today I jump.

questions.q: Yesterday we … to the park.
questions.explain: Yesterday we walked to the park.

questions.q: Tomorrow I … my granny.
questions.explain: Tomorrow I will visit my granny.

questions.q: Which sentence is happening now?
questions.explain: She is reading. It is happening now.

questions.q: Which word shows the future?
hints: Will tells us it has not happened yet.
questions.explain: Will shows the future.

questions.q: Sort into past and future.
hints: Look for e d or will.
Will cook and will dance are later.
questions.explain: Cooked and danced are past. Will cook and will dance are future.

units.parent: Your child learned how verbs change for past, present and future.
units.teacher: Shows regular past tense with -ed, present tense and future with will.
units.done: Verbs change to show yesterday, today and tomorrow.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Poem: The Year Goes Round
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 English Home Language: Reading and Viewing (read a poem; answer questions; identify rhyming words; make up own rhymes)
units.intention: Today I am reading a poem and finding the rhyming words.
units.prompt: Which season in the poem do you like best?
units.passage:
The Year Goes Round (a 2to.iQ poem)

In summer, the sun is hot and high,
We swim and play below the sky.

In autumn, leaves turn brown and fall,
The wind blows cool across the wall.

In winter, nights are long and cold,
We wear warm jerseys, new and old.

In spring, the flowers start to grow,
And baby birds sing soft and low.

lesson.say: Read the poem, or press Read aloud to hear it.
lesson.html:
The Year Goes Round (a 2to.iQ poem)

In summer, the sun is hot and high,
We swim and play below the sky.

In autumn, leaves turn brown and fall,
The wind blows cool across the wall.

In winter, nights are long and cold,
We wear warm jerseys, new and old.

In spring, the flowers start to grow,
And baby birds sing soft and low.

lesson.say: A poem is written in short lines. A group of lines is called a verse. This poem has four verses, one for each season.
lesson.html:
Summer→Autumn→Winter→Spring

Each verse is about one season.

lesson.say: Poems often rhyme. High rhymes with sky. Fall rhymes with wall.
lesson.html:
high, sky→fall, wall→cold, old→grow, low

Rhyming words sound the same at the end.

steps: Look at the end of the next line.

questions.q: In which season do leaves turn brown and fall?
questions.explain: In autumn, leaves turn brown and fall.

questions.q: What do we wear in winter?
questions.explain: In winter we wear warm jerseys.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with grow?
questions.explain: Grow and low rhyme.

questions.q: How many verses does the poem have?
questions.explain: The poem has 4 verses, one per season.

questions.q: Put the seasons in the order of the poem.
hints: The poem starts with the hot season.
questions.explain: Summer, autumn, winter, spring.

reflect.q: How did you enjoy the poem best?

units.parent: Your child read a poem about the seasons and found rhyming words.
units.teacher: Shows comprehension of a poem, the concept of a verse, and identification of rhyming pairs.
units.done: Poems have verses, and many poems rhyme.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Friends and bullying
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Life Skills, Personal and Social Well-being, Term 1: Myself and others (qualities of friends; sharing, helping, respect; dealing with conflict and bullying)
units.intention: Today I am learning what makes a good friend and what to do about bullying.
units.prompt: What makes you a good friend?

lesson.say: A good friend is kind, shares, listens and helps you.
lesson.html:
🤝 💛 👂

Good friends are kind, fair and helpful.

lesson.say: Bullying is when someone hurts or frightens another person again and again, on purpose.
lesson.html:
😟

Bullying happens on purpose and keeps happening. It is never okay.

lesson.say: If you are bullied or see bullying, tell a grown-up you trust. Telling is not tattling. It keeps people safe.
lesson.html:
Say stop→Walk away→Tell a grown-up

Tell a trusted grown-up, like a teacher or parent.

example.q: Every day, a boy takes Zola's lunch and laughs at her. What should Zola do?
steps: This keeps happening and it is on purpose.
Zola should tell a grown-up she trusts.

questions.q: Which is what a good friend does?
hints: How does a good friend make you feel?
questions.explain: A good friend shares and is kind.

questions.q: Someone is pushing a child at break every day. What is this?
questions.explain: Hurting someone again and again on purpose is bullying.

questions.q: Who can you tell about bullying?
questions.explain: Tell a teacher, parent or another grown-up you trust.

questions.q: You see a new child sitting alone. What could you do?
questions.explain: Inviting them to play is kind.

questions.q: Sort into kind and unkind.
hints: How would the other person feel?
Calling names and taking things hurt.
questions.explain: Helping and sharing are kind.

reflect.q: How do you show you are a good friend?

units.parent: Your child talked about friendship and learned to tell a trusted adult about bullying.
units.teacher: Shows understanding of friendship qualities, recognising bullying and seeking adult help.
units.done: Good friends are kind. Tell a trusted grown-up about bullying.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: The four seasons
units.topic: Seasons and how they change things
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Life Skills, Beginning Knowledge, Term 2: Seasons (the four seasons; effects on people, plants and animals)
units.intention: Today I am learning about the four seasons and how they change our lives.
units.prompt: Which season is it now where you live?

lesson.say: There are four seasons in a year: summer, autumn, winter and spring.
lesson.html:
☀️ 🍂 ❄️ 🌸

Summer→Autumn→Winter→Spring

lesson.say: In South Africa, summer is in December and winter is in June and July. In parts of the country, most rain falls in summer. In the Western Cape, most rain falls in winter.
lesson.html:
December: summer→July: winter

Our seasons are the opposite of countries in the north.

lesson.say: In autumn many trees lose their leaves. In spring, plants grow new leaves and flowers, and many animals have babies.
lesson.html:
🍂 🌳 → 🌸 🐣

Seasons change what plants and animals do.

example.q: It is cold and the days are short. Which season is it?

questions.q: In which month is it summer in South Africa?
questions.explain: December is summer in South Africa.

questions.q: When do many trees lose their leaves?
hints: It is the season before winter.
questions.explain: Many trees lose their leaves in autumn.

questions.q: When do flowers start to bloom?
questions.explain: Flowers bloom in spring.

questions.q: Put the seasons in order, starting with summer.
questions.explain: Summer, autumn, winter, spring.

questions.q: What do we wear?
hints: Summer is hot, winter is cold.
Scarves and gloves keep us warm.
Shorts and sun hats are for hot days.
questions.explain: Shorts and sun hats for summer. Scarf and gloves for winter.

reflect.q: Which season do you like best?

units.parent: Your child learned the four seasons and how they change weather, plants, animals and clothes.
units.teacher: Shows naming and sequencing the seasons and describing their effects on people, plants and animals.
units.done: The four seasons change our weather, plants and animals.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Animal homes
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Life Skills, Beginning Knowledge, Term 2: Animal homes (creatures that build, find or carry their homes); Animals that live in water
units.intention: Today I am learning how animals build, find or carry their homes.

lesson.say: Some animals build their homes. Birds build nests. Weaver birds weave nests from grass. Bees build a hive.
lesson.html:
🪺 🐝

Birds build nests. Bees build hives.

lesson.say: Some animals find a home. A bat finds a cave. A meerkat lives in a burrow under the ground.
lesson.html:
🦇 🕳️

Animals can find caves, holes and trees to live in.

lesson.say: Some animals carry their homes on their backs. A snail and a tortoise carry their shells.
lesson.html:
🐌 🐢

A shell is a home you can carry.

example.q: A hermit crab lives in an empty shell and moves to a bigger one when it grows. Does it build, find or carry its home?
steps: It does not make the shell.
It finds an empty shell, and takes it with it.
It finds and carries its home.

questions.q: What home does a bird build?
questions.explain: Birds build nests.

questions.q: Which animal carries its home?
hints: Its home is on its back.
questions.explain: A tortoise carries its shell.

questions.q: Where does a meerkat live?
options: In a burrow under the ground
hints: Their home is under the ground.
questions.explain: Meerkats live in burrows.

questions.q: Sort the animals.
questions.explain: Weaver birds and bees build. Snails and tortoises carry.

questions.q: Which animal lives in the sea?
questions.explain: An octopus lives in the sea.

reflect.q: Which animal home would you like to see?

units.parent: Your child learned how animals build, find or carry their homes.
units.teacher: Shows classification of animal homes as built, found or carried, and identifying a water creature.
units.done: Animals build, find or carry their homes.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Road safety
units.topic: Crossing the road and road signs
units.caps: CAPS Grade 2 Life Skills, Personal and Social Well-being, Term 3: Road safety (rules for pedestrians and passengers; road signs; scholar patrols)
units.intention: Today I am learning how to stay safe on the road.
units.prompt: What will you do the next time you cross a road?

lesson.say: Before you cross, stop at the side of the road. Look right, look left and look right again. Listen for cars.
lesson.html:
Stop→Look right→Look left→Look right→Listen

Cross only when the road is clear. Walk, do not run.

lesson.say: Cross at a pedestrian crossing, at a traffic light when the green man shows, or where a scholar patrol helps you.
lesson.html:
🚸 🚦 🧍

Green man means you may cross. Red man means wait.

lesson.say: In a car, always wear your seatbelt. Get in and out on the side of the pavement, not the road.
lesson.html:
🚗 🔒

Buckle your seatbelt every time.

example.q: Neo wants to cross the road to the shop. There is a pedestrian crossing a little further on. What should he do?
steps: Stop, look right, left and right again, then cross.

questions.q: What should you do first before crossing?
options: Stop at the side of the road
hints: Stop at the side of the road.
questions.explain: Always stop at the side of the road first.

questions.q: The traffic light shows the red man. What do you do?
questions.explain: Red man means wait.

questions.q: What must you wear in a car?
hints: It keeps you in your seat.
questions.explain: Always wear a seatbelt.

questions.q: Put the steps in order.
items: Look right, left and right again
questions.explain: Stop, look, then cross.

questions.q: Sort into safe and not safe.
hints: Playing in the road and crossing between cars are dangerous.
The green man and seatbelts are safe.
questions.explain: Crossing at the green man and wearing a seatbelt are safe.

units.parent: Your child learned how to cross the road safely and to wear a seatbelt. Practise on your next walk together.
units.teacher: Shows knowledge of pedestrian rules, traffic light signals and passenger safety.
units.done: Stop, look and listen before you cross the road.
